'Building lines when the work order is deleted, built twice, or reopened
'Yes

'With its work order deleted the inspection can no longer be built from at all and its footer offers View PDF only, and a build by someone else is no longer followed by a 'build again?' confirmation because an inspection is built from once.

'Deleted run-on work order: before (22 Sep spec), 'only the option to create a new work order is offered', so the tester saw Build lines (with 'A new work order') and Go to work order. Now (14 Oct spec): 'no build action is offered' and 'the footer offers View PDF only, with or without ShopCoach, and no plain line; it also shows the outcome when the lines went onto another work order that still exists'. Another user building while the screen is open: before, this led to the confirmation to build again; now 'the check' means built once, so nothing is added, the tester is told where the lines went, and the footer then shows the outcome ('WO created S-235' or 'Lines added S-58') instead of Build lines.

'S3-E1: 6 Oct 2026 (Deleted work orders, removed inspections and splits)
S3-R6: 7 Oct 2026 (Deleted work order: outcome, footer, reopened, merge (SV-10965))
S3-E2: 7 Oct 2026 (Leftovers from the built-once rule; file limit; submit name)
S2-R13: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
S3-R8: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)

'If the run-on work order has been deleted, only the option to create a new work order is offered.
If another user builds from the same inspection while this screen is open, the re-build confirmation is based on the current state rather than the state when the screen loaded.

'With the run-on work order deleted, the completed inspection offers no build action at all: no Build lines and no new-work-order option.
Its footer offers View PDF only, with or without ShopCoach: no Go to work order and no line about the work order note feed.
If lines had been built onto another work order that still exists before the deletion, the footer also shows that outcome (for example 'WO created S-235'), linking to it.
If another user adds lines from the same inspection while your screen is open, the check uses the inspection as it is now: nothing is added a second time and you are told where the lines went. No confirmation to build again appears.
After that, the screen no longer offers Build lines; its footer shows the outcome ('WO created …' or 'Lines added …') with a link.

'1. Delete the run-on work order, then open the completed inspection; confirm only 'create a new work order' is offered.
2. In a second browser signed in as another user, build from the same inspection while this screen is still open in the first; check the re-build confirmation reflects the current state, not the state when the screen loaded.

'1. Delete the work order that a completed, not yet built-from inspection with findings was run on.
2. Open the asset's Inspections tab and open that inspection.
3. Check its footer offers View PDF only: no Build lines, no Go to work order and no line about the work order note feed.
4. Complete another inspection with a Not OK finding, press Build lines, choose A new work order and press Add Lines.
5. Delete the work order that inspection was run on (not the new one).
6. Open the asset's Inspections tab and open that inspection.
7. Check its footer offers View PDF and the outcome 'WO created …' linking to the new work order, with no Build lines and no Go to work order.
8. In an organisation without ShopCoach, delete the work order a completed inspection was run on.
9. Open that inspection from the asset's Inspections tab.
10. Check its footer offers View PDF only, with no Go to work order and no plain line about the customer report and the work order note feed.
11. Back in the organisation with ShopCoach, open the completed screen of a third completed inspection with findings in the first browser.
12. In the second browser, signed in as another user, build from the same inspection and press Add Lines.
13. In the first browser, without reloading, press Build lines, choose a target and, if proposed lines appear, press Add Lines.
14. Check nothing is added a second time, you are told where the lines went, and no confirmation to build again appears.
15. Reload the completed screen.
16. Check the footer shows the outcome with a link instead of Build lines.
'Decided by the product manager on 6 and 7 Oct in answer to the developer's questions. Steps 8 to 10 need an organisation without ShopCoach.

'Build lines from the report note, on a phone and on an ineligible work order
'Yes
'For a work order that cannot take lines, the note's Build lines now opens the menu offering only a new work order, instead of creating one without asking.

'The note's own rule still says the build 'creates a new work order ... and the note stays where it is', but the rule it points to changed. Before (22 Sep spec): 'the system will create a new work order without asking', so pressing Build lines on the note of a Complete work order created a new work order straight away. Now (14 Oct spec): 'the destination menu still opens and offers only a new work order', so a menu opens with only 'A new work order' and nothing is created until the user chooses it.
'S2-R5: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
'If the work order is not an eligible build target, the build creates a new work order and the note stays where it is.

'On the note of a work order that is not eligible (Complete, Invoiced, Paid or Declined, or already invoiced), pressing Build lines opens the destination menu; it does not create a work order without asking.
The menu offers only a new work order; this work order is not listed.
Choosing it builds onto a new work order for the same customer and asset, and the note stays where it is (unchanged).
'3. On a note whose work order status is not eligible (Complete, Invoiced, Paid or Declined), check a new work order is created and the note stays put.

'1. On the note whose work order is Complete, Invoiced, Paid or Declined, press Build lines.
2. Check the destination menu opens and offers only a new work order.
3. Choose the new work order.
4. Check a new work order is created for the same customer and asset.
5. Check the note is still on the original work order.

'Decided on 29 Sep. The note rule's own wording did not change; the rule it refers to did. The last expected line (new work order created, note stays put) is unchanged and kept only to finish the flow.

'Building again asks to confirm, based on the inspection as it is now
'No
'Building again from the note with a confirmation is gone: once built from anywhere, the note shows the outcome instead of Build lines, and a stale Add Lines started from the note adds nothing.

'Before (22 Sep spec): on the note of an inspection already built from elsewhere, Build lines was present and pressing it led to a confirmation ('If the inspection was already built from through another entry point, the user is asked to confirm'). Now (14 Oct spec) those rules are deleted and 'Once the inspection has been built from, the note shows the outcome in place of Build lines': there is no Build lines, only a 'WO created …' or 'Lines added …' link, and an Add Lines pressed on lines drafted before the other build adds nothing and says where the lines went.

'S4-R3: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
S4-E2: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
S2-R13: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
S4-R5: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)

'The re-build confirmation is based on the inspection's current state rather than on the note, so a build done elsewhere afterwards still triggers the warning.
If the inspection was already built from through another entry point, the user is asked to confirm.

'The note of an inspection already built from elsewhere does not offer Build lines. In its place it shows the outcome, 'WO created …' or 'Lines added …', linking to the work order that got the lines.
The note shows the inspection as it is now, even though the note was posted before the build.
No confirmation to build again is shown.
If the proposed lines from the note were already open when the other build happened, pressing Add Lines adds nothing and says where the lines went.

'1. From the note, press Build lines on an inspection that has already been built from elsewhere.
2. Confirm the confirmation prompt is based on the inspection's current state rather than on the note's snapshot.

'1. In the first browser tab, open the work order's Notes tab, find the inspection report note, press Build lines, choose This work order and wait for the proposed lines.
2. In a second browser tab, open the same inspection's completed screen, press Build lines, choose a target and press Add Lines.
3. Back in the first tab, press Add Lines.
4. Check nothing is added, a message says where the lines went, and no question asks you to confirm building again.
5. Open the work order's Notes tab and find the inspection report note.
6. Check the note shows the outcome ('WO created …' or 'Lines added …') and no Build lines.
7. Click the outcome link.
8. Check it opens the work order that got the lines.
'Decided on 29 Sep ('an inspection is built from once').

'Inspections tab filters, summary line and needs-action counts
'Yes
'The filter row was removed (three columns sort instead) and the summary line has new words.

'Before (22 Sep spec): 'A filter row will offer All, Needs action, With issues and Not started, each with a count taken from the full list' and 'A summary will read "N of M need a work order"'. Now (14 Oct spec): 'The table has no filter row. The Inspection, Status and Completed columns can be sorted' and 'A summary will read "N of M have findings with no lines yet"'. The tester now sees no filter row, sortable column headers and different summary words.

'S5-R10: 5 Oct 2026 (Developer and QA questions answered)
S5-R11: between 29 Sep 2026 and 2 Oct 2026 (Not named in the change log; Jira SV-10792 (2 Oct 2026) already quotes the new text)
S5-R12: 7 Oct 2026 (Filter leftovers removed)

'A filter row offers All, Needs action, With issues and Not started, each count taken from the full list rather than the filtered view.
A summary reads "N of M need a work order".
An inspection needs action when it was completed after this release, has at least one Monitor or Not OK finding, and has not been built from; a pre-release inspection is never flagged but stays reachable under With issues.

'The tab has no filter row: no All, Needs action, With issues or Not started.
The Inspection, Status and Completed columns can be sorted.
The summary reads "N of M have findings with no lines yet".

'1. Read the filter row (All, Needs action, With issues, Not started) and confirm each count is taken from the full list, not the filtered view.
2. Read the summary 'N of M need a work order'.
3. Confirm an inspection shows Needs action only when it was completed after this release, has a Monitor or Not OK finding, and has not been built from; a pre-release inspection is never flagged but stays reachable under With issues.

'1. Open the asset's Inspections tab.
2. Check there is no filter row.
3. Click the Inspection column header and check the list sorts.
4. Click the Status column header and check the list sorts.
5. Click the Completed column header and check the list sorts.
6. Read the summary line and check it reads 'N of M have findings with no lines yet'.

'The filter row was removed on 5 Oct. The new summary wording has no change-log entry; it first appears in a developer task on 2 Oct. The 22 Sep design already showed no filter chips and the new summary wording, but the 22 Sep spec did not, and the case followed the spec. The default order (most recently completed first) and the rule that a pre-release inspection is never flagged are unchanged and are left out.
